correctness.rationale: Under weights 1,2,3, F(0)=0 and every increment F(k)−F(k−1) lies in {1,2,3}: extend a maximizing shorter factor by one letter, or truncate a maximizing longer factor. Splitting a factor gives subadditivity F(i+k)≤F(i)+F(k); thus the word formed from the increments has each factor weight F(i+k)−F(i)≤F(k), with equality on the prefix. This proves existence and uniqueness of the normal form in the exact regime used. Equal length and F(n) force the displacement (t,−2t,t). Orient t>0: F(1)=3 forces a c in the lower-c word, which also needs ≥2t b's. Then n≥2t+1. For odd n=2r+1, equality t=r would force count vectors (0,2r,1) versus (r,0,r+1), with maximum length-two weight 5 versus an even value, impossible. For sharpness subtract weight 2 from every letter. The witness core c(ac)^(r−1), of length 2r−1, alternates +1 and −1, starting and ending +1. It attains +1 at every odd length up to the core length. The preceding b (deviation 0) plus an odd core prefix attains +1 at every even length through 2r. All factors have deviation ≤1. The additional initial a in the odd case has deviation −1 and makes the full-length deviation 0 without affecting these proper-length maxima. This gives the displayed normal-form prefixes and Parikh-distance 4(r−1), including the zero endpoints n=2 and n=3. The finite replay independently confirms the expected sequence, but is not used to infer the infinite result.
residual_risks: Proof is for standard ternary weights and n≥2; no assertion for other measures or alphabets or for classification of all maximizing pairs.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the n=4 witness and qualitative noninvariance to the original authors. The supported distinct assertion is the global sharp all-length bound, including arbitrary equivalent pairs and all lengths of attainment; it does not follow from a single example or general form existence.

evidence: Standard weights on ordered letters are 1,2,3, and the relevant profile consists of the maximum contiguous factor weights at every length. Related indexed Tribonacci and 2-automatic records study counts of possible sums or Parikh vectors of factors in specified infinite words.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Equality of the entire maximal-weight profile, not total weight or abelian complexity, is the hypothesis. The two complexity questions do not imply an extremal displacement in an equivalence class. The class diameter here is four times the maximum c-count spread.

It explicitly leaves exact Parikh-vector behavior open. No checked statement implies the all-length bound with matching witnesses for each length, or the stronger bound on every pair within a class. checked_sources: Frozen extremal theorem and its symbolic upper bound and sharp witnesses
value.rationale: This measures exactly how much Parikh information the canonical weighted normalization can lose in the smallest alphabet that permits such loss. The bound answers a quantitative version of the original paper's identified question at every length and, as a class-diameter bound, applies independently of which representative is used. It has parity-sensitive sharpness, with explicit infinite families, rather than merely showing a change is possible.
residual_risks: Does not characterize full equivalence classes or how the diameter depends on an individual factor-weight profile.
